questions.q: Using only ruler and compass, which of the following angles is constructible according to the Exemplar examples?
questions.explanation: A 75-degree angle can be obtained by combining standard constructible angles 45 degrees and 30 degrees. Bisecting 75 degrees gives 37.5 degrees. Therefore 37.5 degrees is constructible using ruler and compass.

questions.q: Why is an angle of 67.5 degrees constructible with ruler and compass?
options: A) Because it is one-third of 202.5 degrees.
B) Because it is half of 135 degrees, and 135 degrees can be formed from 90 degrees and 45 degrees.
C) Because every decimal angle is constructible.
D) Because it is the supplement of 22.5 degrees only.
questions.answer: B) Because it is half of 135 degrees, and 135 degrees can be formed from 90 degrees and 45 degrees.
questions.explanation: The Exemplar writes 67.5 degrees as 135/2 degrees. A 135-degree angle can be constructed as 90 degrees + 45 degrees. Bisecting that angle gives 67.5 degrees.

questions.q: A triangle ABC is to be constructed with BC = 3 cm, angle C = 60 degrees, and the difference AB - AC specified. Which listed difference makes the construction possible?
questions.explanation: For a triangle, the absolute difference of two sides must be less than the third side. Here the fixed side BC is 3 cm, so the specified difference AB - AC must be less than 3 cm. Among the options, only 2.8 cm satisfies that condition.

questions.q: A triangle is proposed with angle B = 105 degrees, angle C = 90 degrees, and perimeter 10 cm. Why is the construction impossible?
options: A) The perimeter is too small for every triangle.
B) A right angle cannot be used in ruler-and-compass construction.
C) The two given angles must be equal.
D) The two given angles already sum to 195 degrees, exceeding the 180-degree angle sum of a triangle.
questions.answer: D) The two given angles already sum to 195 degrees, exceeding the 180-degree angle sum of a triangle.
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle must add to exactly 180 degrees. Here 105 + 90 = 195 degrees before the third angle is even included. Therefore no triangle with these two angles exists, regardless of the stated perimeter.
